editorial.headline: Lighter Manufacturing Is Nationally Open, But Bali Blocks PMA Registration
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 32908 covers the manufacture of metal and plastic lighters; nationally it is open to foreign ownership, but Bali blocks PMA registration under its risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 32908 is a narrow manufacturing code: it covers the making of various kinds of lighters, using metal or plastic as the base material. The record does not limit the activity to one operating technology. It includes lighters operated mechanically, electrically, or through another mechanism. In plain English, this is the industrial production of lighter products, not retail, distribution, import, repair, or a broader household-goods category.

The activity is open across the full scale range listed in the record: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar**. That matters because the code is not reserved in the slim record for only one class of operator. A small producer and a large manufacturer sit under the same activity description if what they are doing is the manufacture of lighter products from metal or plastic. The record gives no separate process threshold, output volume, factory-size test, licence condition, or capital number, so none should be read into it.

Nationally, the investment picture is clean. The PMA status is **TERBUKA**, with **pma_max_asing** recorded as **100** under **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national record presents this activity as open up to a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. There is no partial national cap in the slim record, and there is no additional national qualification stated here beyond the code, the activity scope, the scale availability, and the cited PMA source.

Bali is the decisive complication. The same record marks the Bali side as **Blocked (risk class)**, with **l4_bali_blocked** set to true. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale **Besar** is **Rendah/Menengah-Rendah** on every scope, so the activity is blocked by the Bali moratorium dated May 13, 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is broader and sharper: Bali province blocks **all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA**, island-wide and permanently, with the source given as **Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP**. So the honest reading is not that the code is unclear, or that Bali has a separate foreign-share percentage. The honest reading is that KBLI 32908 is nationally open to PMA, but a foreigner cannot register it as a PMA activity in Bali today under the Bali rule recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 32908 is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, but Bali blocks PMA registration for it under the risk-class moratorium recorded in the file.
